elements.title: Valencia Theatre (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that New York City's Valencia Theatre (pictured) was sold to a church in 1977 for $1?

elements.title: Corinne Rey-Bellet (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the murder of skier Corinne Rey-Bellet led to a change in Swiss gun-control regulations?

elements.title: Home and Beauty (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Home and Beauty has been described as both a "little masterpiece of polite merriment" and a "misogynist comedy dipped in vitriol"?

elements.title: Bea Hines (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Bea Hines, the first African-American woman to become a reporter at the Miami Herald, was sent to report on a riot on her first day at work?

elements.title: al-Moghraqa (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that terracotta cones found at al-Moghraqa in Palestine are unique in the region, but resemble artefacts from ancient Egypt?

elements.title: Yvonne Francis-Gibson (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Yvonne Francis-Gibson, before improving women's rights as a legislator in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, led a Women's Desk that was "unable to take a firm stand on behalf of women's issues"?

elements.title: Aquilegia moorcroftiana (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Aquilegia moorcroftiana is named after a mountaineer and is found at the highest elevation of any species of columbine?

elements.title: was just one center (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention was just one center until 1980?

elements.title: Shikairo Days (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Yuki Waga created the "earworm" for "Shikairo Days" by walking around his house repeating "shikanoko nokonoko koshitantan"?
